mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (كيف فعل ربك): (كيف) is an adverb, and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is (فعل). (تر) does not govern it, because it contains the meaning of interrogation, and what precedes it does not govern it. Because of its resemblance to the alif [Translator's note: i.e. the interrogative hamza] it is indeclinable (mabnī), and it is built on the fatḥa because of the quiescence of what precedes it, and because the kasra after the yāʾ is heavy. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «ولأنه ياء الكسر بعد الياء ثقيله», which is garbled; it has been rendered according to its evident sense.]

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (أبابيل): its singular is «إبّول», like «عجّول» and «عجاجيل»; and it was said: its singular is «إبّيل», like «سكّين» and «سكاكين»; and it was said: its singular is «إبّال», like «دينار» and «دنانير» — the origin of «دينار» being «دنّار», the proof of which is the repetition of the nūn in the plural and the diminutive. And it was said: it is a plural that has no singular; and it was said: it is a collective noun (ism li-l-jamʿ).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (ترميهم): in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of (طير); likewise (أبابيل) is a naʿt of (طير), as though He said: scattered groups.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (كعصف): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, the second object of (جعل), because it has the meaning of «صيّر» (made into).
